title: Pregnancy-linked work interruption can produce a quantified reinstatement order while durable restoration remains unverified
source_unit: Fair Work Commission decision [2025] FWC 3646 concerning Kaur v Adecco Industrial Australia Pty Ltd
geography: Australia; Amazon-site labour-supply employment and Fair Work Commission proceeding

observations.period: Pregnancy disclosure through December 19, 2025; work interruption, alternative employment, worker response, and remedy deadline

work_interruption.value: After pregnancy disclosure and lifting restrictions, regular shifts and training were withdrawn and employment was placed on hold; the Commission found the dismissal unfair

prior_work_and_loss.value: The worker had regular full-time hours and an average prior earning rate of $1,426 per week; regular work and expected wages were interrupted

worker_response_and_alternative.value: The worker pushed back by SMS and email, requested accommodation or training, filed the application, and worked for another employer for two weeks during the lost-remuneration period
worker_response_and_alternative.unit: reported response and bounded alternative-work sequence

remedy_order.value: The Commission ordered reinstatement to the former position with continuity by December 19, 2025 and payment of $14,830.40 less tax plus superannuation

receipt_and_durability.unit: missing payment receipt, payroll evidence, actual reinstatement, shifts worked, recurrence, later employment, household recovery, trust, and exit

mechanism.value: A pregnancy-linked interruption can be legally corrected with a quantified reinstatement and lost-pay order while the worker's actual return, payment receipt, and durable work security remain separate open stages

observations.method: Structured extraction from the official Fair Work Commission decision; pregnancy disclosure, work interruption, worker response, alternative employment, quantified remedy, and open implementation are kept separate.
observations.uncertainty: The decision is a selected adjudicated case, not a prevalence estimate. It does not retain private claimant, payroll, medical, household, alternative-job, or post-deadline compliance records.
observations.subgroup: One worker in an Australian labour-supply employment case involving pregnancy and lifting restrictions; no comparison group or population denominator is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: A temporary hold may be described by the employer as an accommodation or safety process, and taking another job does not establish equivalent pay, commute, choice, or durability; formal remedy is not verified restoration.

boundary: This record establishes one adjudicated case from pregnancy-linked work interruption through bounded alternative employment, worker action, and quantified institutional remedy. It does not establish post-order implementation, payment receipt, restored work, discrimination prevalence, household recovery, trust, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project event ledger derived from the public FWC decision; claimant, payroll, medical, household, and compliance files are not retained.
